relationToMeasurementBridge.independentSurface: signal-lab-tx-stream-v1 is a separately versioned SignalLab-owned host-tooling surface; contracts/signal-lab-measurement-bridge-v1/v2/v3.json and contracts/trio-composition-v4..v7.json are unchanged and remain byte-frozen
relationToMeasurementBridge.measurementEdgeUnchanged: acquireIq remains a bounded single-buffer measurement acquisition of at most 65,536 samples with one synchronous call per result; no streaming method exists on the measurement service
relationToMeasurementBridge.trioLivenessScoping: This contract reads trio-composition-v7 liveness item 3 (no SignalLab child process, framing loop, pipe, or shutdown acknowledgement exists) as governing the in-process measurement service admitted over the SignalLab-to-Atomizer edge; the Tx stream device transport introduced by this contract is an operator-launched host-tool subprocess outside trio composition, with bounded SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL teardown and idempotent dispose
relationToMeasurementBridge.driverEvolutionIntact: trio-composition-v7 compatibility.driverEvolution requires a new instrument/API contract version for complex-IQ chunking, backpressure, or long-lived sample streaming; that requirement remains intact for any Atomizer-facing instrument surface; this contract is host tooling, not an instrument or API contract, registers no driver, and adds no Atomizer-facing capability
relationToMeasurementBridge.stimulusSinkUnchanged: streaming does not activate the reserved SignalLab-to-Firmware stimulus sink and does not change firmwareStimulusSinkStatus

streamModel.continuity: every output sample is a pure function of the plan and its absolute output sample coordinate; any partition of a sample range into consecutive chunks yields byte-identical concatenation and a stream resumed from any disclosed coordinate reproduces the tail exactly
streamModel.cursor: absolute output sample index; derived native coordinates are exact rationals reduced in BigInt with a 40-digit fail-closed representability probe at every chunk boundary before synthesis
streamModel.backpressure: the producer generates the next chunk only after the sink acknowledges the previous one; no unbounded internal queue exists
streamModel.overrunUnderrun: sinks report device counters where available; device underrun detection on libiio 0.25 clients is a client-exit-and-stderr heuristic and is disclosed as such until device-side counters are probed
streamModel.cancellation: explicit cancel or process signal; bounded teardown; the manifest records completed, terminated, or faulted

ci16leConvention.disclosure: The Neptune P210 TX DAC scan format is le:S16/16>>0 per the live unit diagnostic (Atom-NeptuneSDR-Firmware/docs/live-unit/extracted/vendor-diagnostic-report.txt, TX output channels voltage0/voltage1); host quantization is full 16-bit. le:S12/16>>0 with full-scale code 2048 is the RX-direction ADC format and is not the TX convention. Emitted amplitude is controlled only via the hardwaregain attribute; no amplitude verification exists for this surface yet. The live Tx runbook plans an RX-loopback amplitude gate; until that gate executes and records evidence, emitted amplitude must never be inferred from this convention.

qualificationPassthrough.rule: streamed bytes carry the source qualification of their profile or recipe at the chosen rate and phase unchanged; chunk receipts declare the same payload-kind lineage as the measurement bridge and content-bound qualifications apply only to exact native untransformed chunks
qualificationPassthrough.hardwareReadyLimitation: hardware-ready describes deterministic output sample geometry only and never claims DAC behavior, analog reconstruction, antenna coupling, calibrated RF emission, RF conformance, product qualification, or certification
qualificationPassthrough.sourceCleanDisclosure: streamed recipe and profile bytes are source-clean: no propagation channel and no receiver impairment is applied, unlike classifier corpus rows which carry the propagation channel

customProfileStreaming.descriptorResolution: custom-lte, custom-nr, and custom-wifi plans resolve geometry through the pure buildCustomWaveformDescriptor(standard, selections) path and reject illegal pins before any synthesis
customProfileStreaming.moduleStateDisclosure: custom-profile synthesis installs the plan's validated selections into the builder's module state for the duration of each synthesized window (descriptor resolution and generator dispatch both read that state) and restores the prior state immediately afterwards; windows are synthesized synchronously, so interleaved streams each render their own configuration; other same-process consumers of the custom descriptor surfaces observe the installed selections only while a window is being synthesized

recipeDisclosureRequirements: every scheduled recipe states that transitions are sample-domain hard edges
every scheduled recipe states that no power ramp is modeled, including the absent GSM power-time template and the absent Wi-Fi TX ramp
every scheduled recipe states that wideband splatter is expected at schedule edges
every scheduled recipe states that the stream is not representative of a conformant transmitter's spectrum
every recipe states what is standards-consistent, what is engineering choice, what is explicitly absent, and that no canonical artifact exists because the timeline is unbounded

recipes.schedule: corpus schedule as-is: TS0 seeded xCCH 4-frame block cycle plus fixed dummy bursts TS1-7; period 4 frames = 24000 samples; content rotates per cycle. The pinned 1.3 MHz rate is below the P210 device-window floor (2083333 Hz), so this recipe is file/stdio-only; device streaming uses the gsm-900-loaded-bcch profile upsampled into the device window
continuous 10 ms frames; PDSCH content rotates per absolute frame ordinal
continuous 20 ms artifact frames (4x the 5 ms TDD pattern); content rotates per absolute frame ordinal; TDD pattern phase from the absolute coordinate
absolute-PPDU-ordinal schedule: PPDU k at prevEnd + DIFS(680 samples) + backoff(k)*slot(180 samples) with seeded backoff; not a MAC: no ACK, CSMA, or contention resolution
continuous closed-form FM-MPX stereo composite, 256 kHz Carson bandwidth; any sample independently evaluable
continuous voiced full-carrier AM, 10 kHz bandwidth; any sample independently evaluable
